case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
1. Session Summary & Current Stability
General Well-Being: Client presented as reserved initially but engaged well throughout the session. Client reported that things are going "fine" both at home and within the current program environment.
Primary Goal/Challenge: Client identified saving money to reinstate their driver's license as their primary focus over the past week. Client plans to save paychecks over the next week or two to pay for license reinstatement.
Pro-Social Thinking & Risk Management: Discussed past legal issues involving motorcycles and evading law enforcement. Client has access to two motorcycles (via family) once licensed. Client demonstrated insight into past high-risk behaviors (e.g., driving without a license or carrying contraband) and stated a commitment to maintaining their license by avoiding illegal activity and complying with traffic stops.
2. Employment & Vocational Readiness
Timeline: Client is currently in Week 3 of the program and feels ready to begin applying for jobs after Week 4.
Work History & Skills: Client has approximately 1.5 to 2 years of experience operating forklifts, loading trailers, and setting reefer units (1 year at Cargill and 5–6 months at Southeastern Salvage).
Vocational Interests:
Forklift/Warehouse: Interested in higher-paying roles at International Paper, Sysco ($26–$29/hr range noted), or returning to Cargill.
Welding: Client expressed interest in entry-level welding or trade schooling in West Columbia. Client noted they already own personal welding equipment/gear.
Certification Barrier: Client noted that while previous employers trained them on forklifts, they never received a physical certificate or certification number required by many applications.
3. Action Plan & Next Steps
Case Manager Tasks:
Coordinate with "TV" to schedule a trip to Charleston within the next couple of weeks for the client (alongside peers) to obtain official forklift certification.
Research welding job openings/programs in West Columbia and reach out to local industry contact once internet access is restored.
Begin active job application assistance with the client following Week 4.
Client Tasks:
Continue saving funds from upcoming paychecks to complete driver's license reinstatement.
Maintain stability at home and in the program.
Reach out to Case Manager or "Turn 90" staff if immediate needs arise.

case_notes.note_type: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting
case_notes.content:
Session Summary
Driver’s License & Legal Compliance: Discussed steps toward license reinstatement. The client acknowledges outstanding tickets and reinstatement fees and plans to visit the DMV to clarify requirements. The client discussed the risk of operating a vehicle/motorcycle without a valid license, recognizing past patterns and the severe legal penalties if caught.
Community Services & Referrals:
LRADAC: The client has not contacted LRADAC yet due to waiting on funds for transportation. The case manager emphasized the waitlist and encouraged calling early. Clarified that program participation counts toward community service hours.
Dental Clinic: Client intends to follow up with the dental clinic next Friday, depending on schedule and transportation.
Class Application & Emotional Regulation: Client reflected on the current class, noting efforts to pause before reacting, identify emotional triggers, and manage daily boredom constructively around the house.
Transportation & Social Support: Transportation remains the primary barrier to appointments and job opportunities. Client relies on family rides and plans to use rideshares once employed. Client stated they have cut ties with negative peer influences and keep company with employed, pro-social peers.
Employment & Training Goals:
Certifications: Client is prioritizing forklift certification (program outings occur roughly monthly) and completed the introductory HVAC module. Expressed interest in taking the EPA 608 certification exam via SkillCat.
Resume Updates: Reviewed work history for resume revision and future Indeed applications. Confirmed work at Cargil (approx. 2018–2019) and Southeastern Salvage (approx. May–November 2016). Agreed to remove a brief high school retail role (Bi-Lo, 2011).
Taxes/W-2s: Client inquired about filing past W-2s from Southeastern Salvage; case manager agreed to look into retrieval methods.
Action Steps & Plan
Client:
Call LRADAC to join the waiting list and start community service paperwork.
Visit the DMV (targeted for next Friday) to review outstanding fees and requirements.
Attend dental clinic walk-in hours as schedule permits.
Continue coursework on SkillCat toward EPA certification.
Case Manager:
Finalize and format updated resume with specific employment months.
Provide information regarding online W-2 lookup options.
Coordinate forklift certification trip when the next monthly slot opens.
Assist client with SkillCat navigation and Indeed profile setup.
